study.title: The Love That Gives
study.focus: What does God's gift of his Son tell us about the heart of God?
study.take: This take is the short shape: six passages, two for each verse. The passages chosen here converge on the main line: God gives the Son to rescue (3:16), Christ comes to save rather than condemn (3:17), and the one who believes is not condemned (3:18).
study.question: Christ came to heal, not to condemn. What does believing in him look like for you this week?
study.closing: The passages in this study point the same way: the Son was given to rescue, and the one who believes is not condemned. The gift is already offered; believing is how it is received.

scripture.16: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
scripture.17: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.
scripture.18: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the only born Son of God.

summaries.MHC3.16.05: Matthew Henry invites us to be amazed that the great and holy God would love a worthless and wicked world with a love of good will, even though he could take no pleasure in what the world had become. He adds that some Jews wrongly thought the Messiah came only in love for their own nation, but Christ says he came in love for the whole world, Gentiles as well as Jews.
summaries.CHR3.16.1.01: Chrysostom hears Jesus saying: do not be shocked that I must be lifted up so that you may be saved. This pleases the Father, who loved you enough to give his Son for slaves, and ungrateful ones at that. Chrysostom notes that a person would hardly do this even for a friend, or readily for a good person. He adds that Jesus speaks briefly here, yet every word carries weight.
summaries.AUG3.17-18.1.01: Augustine says that, as far as it is up to the physician, Christ came to heal the sick, and a patient who will not follow the physician's orders destroys himself. Christ is called the Saviour of the world because he came to save the world, not to judge it; the one who refuses to be saved by him is judged by himself.
summaries.CAL3.17.02: John Calvin says John repeats the word world so that no one who keeps to the road of faith will think himself shut out. Calvin reads judge here as condemn, and says this shows the real purpose of Christ's coming: there was no need for him to come to destroy people who were already ruined.
summaries.MHC3.18.01: Matthew Henry draws out the happiness of believers. Although a person has been a great sinner and stands convicted, once he believes the process is stopped and judgment is held back. This is more than a delay: he is acquitted and discharged, and is not dealt with by the strict justice his sins deserve.
summaries.JFB3.18.01: Jamieson, Fausset and Brown say the believer has passed from death to life the moment he believes. The one who is condemned already is the one who rejects the single way out that God gave his Son to provide, and so chooses to stay condemned.
